events.title: God tells Jacob to go up to Bethel
events.narrative_summary: God tells Jacob to arise, go up to Bethel, dwell there and make an altar to the God who appeared to him when he fled from Esau.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word. Anchored on the end of the rebuke in Gen 34:30-31, with a 1-day offset and a 2-day margin, since the text just continues the story after Shechem. DAY_SEQUENCE like the chapter 34 events.

events.title: Jacob has his household give up foreign gods
events.narrative_summary: Jacob orders his household to put away foreign gods, purify themselves and change clothes. They hand over their idols and earrings and Jacob buries them under the oak at Shechem.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the command with no delay (35:2 'Then Jacob said'). Gathering and burying take a few hours, 4 hours, with a margin of 6 hours.

events.title: Jacob's company travels to Bethel unpursued
events.narrative_summary: They set out, and the terror of God keeps the surrounding cities from pursuing them. Jacob and all his people come to Luz, which is Bethel.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: urim travel Shechem to Bethel: 33 km straight, about 41 km by road, donkey 4 km/h, 10.2 h moving, about 1 day. A company with flocks and children would take about one day, so duration 1 day, margin 6 hours.

events.title: Jacob builds an altar at Bethel and names the place
events.narrative_summary: Jacob builds an altar at Bethel and calls the place El-Bethel, because God revealed himself to him there when he fled from his brother.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows arrival (35:7), the command of 35:1 and the vow of 35:3 carried out. A few hours after arrival; margin 1 day for setting up camp.

events.title: Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, dies and is buried under an oak
events.narrative_summary: Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, dies and is buried below Bethel under an oak, which is called Allon-bacuth.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word. Placed by verse order after the altar, 3 days later with a 3-day margin. DAY_SEQUENCE like the other Bethel events, which this scene falls among; the 3-day offset and margin are estimates. Burial takes 1 day.

events.title: God appears to Jacob again and renames him Israel
events.narrative_summary: God appears again to Jacob as he comes from Paddan-aram, blesses him, and says his name will no longer be Jacob but Israel.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Again' (35:9) ties it to the visit at Bethel; no time word. Anchored 1 day after Deborah's burial with a 2-day margin, by verse order.

events.title: God promises Jacob nations, kings and the land
events.narrative_summary: God, speaking as God Almighty, tells Jacob to be fruitful, promises a nation and a company of nations, kings from his loins, and the land given to Abraham and Isaac; then God goes up from him.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: A continuation of the same speech (35:11 'And God said to him'): starts when the renaming ends. 30 minutes.

events.title: Jacob sets up a stone pillar and pours offerings on it
events.narrative_summary: Jacob sets up a stone pillar where God spoke with him, pours out a drink offering and oil on it, and names the place Bethel.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows God's departure at once (35:13-14); about 2 hours.

events.title: Rachel goes into hard labour near Ephrath
events.narrative_summary: They leave Bethel, and a short way before Ephrath Rachel goes into hard labour; the midwife tells her not to fear, for she has another son.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: They 'journeyed from Bethel' with no stated delay. urim travel Bethel to Bethlehem: 25 km straight, 31 km by road, donkey about 7.5 hours; the labour is 'a little way' short of Ephrath. Offset 30 hours after the pillar (some time at Bethel plus about 6 hours on the road), margin 2 days.

events.title: Rachel dies bearing Benjamin and is buried
events.narrative_summary: As her life departs Rachel names her son Ben-oni, but Jacob calls him Benjamin. Rachel dies and is buried on the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: She dies in the same labour (35:18), so the event follows the labour's end directly. The burial is the same day, 1 day in all.

events.title: Jacob sets up a pillar over Rachel's grave
events.narrative_summary: Jacob sets up a pillar over Rachel's grave, which is still its marker 'to this day'.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word; a day after the burial for the work, 2-day margin.

events.title: Israel moves on and pitches his tent beyond Migdal-eder
events.narrative_summary: Israel travels on and pitches his tent beyond the tower of Eder.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Bethlehem to the tower of Eder is about 2 km straight, so it takes under an hour. Offset 1 day after the pillar, margin 2 days for mourning; no time word.

events.title: Reuben lies with Bilhah and Israel hears of it
events.narrative_summary: While Israel dwells in that land, Reuben goes and lies with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and Israel hears of it.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'When Israel dwelt in that land' gives no interval. I estimate 2 months after Eder, margin 2 months. MACRO_ERA because the text gives no time.

events.title: Jacob comes to his father Isaac at Mamre
events.narrative_summary: Jacob comes to his father Isaac at Mamre, Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac lived as sojourners.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No interval stated. 6 months after the previous scene, with a 6-month margin. The journey Eder to Hebron is about 24 km straight, a day by donkey. Must be before Joseph is 17 (Gen 37:14).

events.title: Isaac dies at 180 and Esau and Jacob bury him
events.narrative_summary: Isaac lives 180 years, dies old and full of days, and is gathered to his people. Esau and Jacob, his sons, bury him.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Age 180 (35:28): offset 180 years from anchor.isaac_birth, margin 1 year since an age covers the whole year. About 1886 BCE. Burial takes about a day. Told here out of time order (see Ramban on 35:28).
events.ancient_year_marker: The days of Isaac were a hundred and eighty years

causal_edges.causal_explanation: Jacob does what God commanded in 35:1 and builds the altar at Bethel (35:7).
Jacob prepares his household for the trip to Bethel that God ordered, purging idols first (35:1-2).
Jacob marks Rachel's burial place with a pillar after she dies (35:19-20).
Rachel's hard labour ends in her death as she bears Benjamin (35:16-18).

entities.etymology_meaning: Mizbeach means 'place of slaughter or offering'; the place is named El-Bethel, 'the God of Bethel'.
entities.summary_bio: The altar Jacob builds at Bethel in obedience to God's command (35:1). He names the place El-Bethel because God revealed himself there when he fled from Esau.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew nezamim, rings worn in the ear or nose; in the ancient Near East such rings often carried amuletic or cultic meaning.
entities.summary_bio: The rings the household wore in their ears, handed to Jacob together with the foreign gods. He buries them under the oak by Shechem, which suggests they were connected with the idolatry being given up.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew 'the gods of the foreign (land)'; nekhar means what is alien or foreign.
entities.summary_bio: The idols that Jacob's household and the people with him carried out of Paddan-aram and picked up at Shechem. At Jacob's command they hand them over and he buries them under the oak by Shechem before the journey to Bethel.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew matsevah, a standing stone set up as a memorial or cultic marker.
entities.summary_bio: The stone pillar Jacob sets up at Bethel where God spoke with him, pouring a drink offering and oil on it. It echoes the pillar he anointed on his flight (28:18), though the text does not say it is the same stone.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew 'pillar of the grave of Rachel'.
entities.summary_bio: The memorial stone Jacob sets up over Rachel's grave on the road to Ephrath. The narrator says it stood 'to this day', so the monument was known to the later audience.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew 'the cities which are around them'; a collective for the Canaanite towns near Shechem.
entities.summary_bio: The Canaanite towns around Shechem who might have avenged the massacre of Shechem. Terror from God falls on them as Jacob's company leaves, and they do not pursue.
The oak below Bethel where Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, was buried. It took its name from the mourning for her.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew 'house of bread'; Ephrath probably means 'fruitful'.
entities.summary_bio: The town on whose approach Rachel gave birth and died; the text glosses the way to Ephrath as Bethlehem. Rachel was buried by the road and Jacob set a pillar over her grave.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew elah, a large tree, traditionally rendered oak or terebinth; the definite article marks a well-known tree.
entities.summary_bio: A tree near Shechem where Jacob hides the household's foreign gods and earrings. It is probably the same landmark as the oak of Moreh, where Abraham first built an altar in Canaan.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew 'tower of the flock', probably a shepherds' watchtower.
entities.summary_bio: A watchtower south of Bethlehem near which Israel pitches his tent after burying Rachel. Micah 4:8 later uses the name of a place for Jerusalem's future.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew meyaledet, 'one who helps in birth'; no personal name is given.
entities.summary_bio: The unnamed midwife who attends Rachel in her hard labour near Ephrath. She tells Rachel not to fear because she is bearing another son.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew nesekh, from the root 'to pour out'.
entities.summary_bio: A liquid poured out in worship. Jacob pours it on the pillar at Bethel together with oil; this is the first libation recorded in the Bible.

systems.name: Terror from God
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Texts of the region often describe a god casting terror or panic on enemies, so that an army or a population flees or fails to fight. In Israel's tradition this is a way that God fights or protects without an army (Exod 15:16; 23:27; 2 Chr 14:14).
rules_and_mechanics: God causes fear to fall on a people.
The terror acts in place of a military defence.
The people afraid refrain from attack or pursuit.
It protects God's people while they carry out his command.

systems.name: Ritual purification
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Throughout the ancient Near East, approaching a deity or a holy place required washing and clean clothing. The practice marks the transition from ordinary life to sacred space, and in Israel it is later regulated in the Priestly law.
rules_and_mechanics: Items or practices tied to other gods are removed first.
The participants wash or cleanse themselves.
They change their garments before approaching the sacred place.
The head of the household gives the command and the whole household obeys.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Jacob builds an altar at Bethel.
system_instances.significance_note: It carries out God's command (35:1) and Jacob's own promise at 35:3.

system_instances.outcome_summary: As she dies, Rachel names her newborn Ben-oni, 'son of my sorrow'.
system_instances.significance_note: It records the cost of the birth and the last act of Rachel's life.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Jacob changes the child's name to Benjamin.
system_instances.significance_note: It turns a name of grief into one of strength or favour, 'son of the right hand'.

system_instances.outcome_summary: God tells Jacob to arise, go up to Bethel, live there and build an altar.
system_instances.significance_note: It ends the unsettled years after Shechem and recalls the vow Jacob made at Bethel.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Jacob names the place El-Bethel, 'the God of Bethel'.
system_instances.significance_note: The name honours the God who revealed himself there when Jacob fled from Esau.

system_instances.outcome_summary: God appears to Jacob once more, on his return from Paddan-aram, and blesses him.
system_instances.significance_note: It confirms the vision of 28:12-15 now that Jacob has returned to the land.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The household gives up its foreign gods and earrings and Jacob buries them under the oak by Shechem.
system_instances.significance_note: It shows Jacob's family putting away idolatry before meeting the God of Bethel.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Esau and Jacob together bury Isaac after his death at 180.
system_instances.significance_note: The brothers, who went separate ways after their meeting in ch. 33 (33:16-17), bury their father together.

system_instances.outcome_summary: God tells Jacob that he will no longer be called Jacob but Israel.
system_instances.significance_note: It reaffirms the name given at Peniel (32:28) and makes it official before the covenant promise.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Jacob sets up a stone pillar, pours a drink offering and oil on it, and names the place Bethel.
system_instances.significance_note: It marks the place of God's speaking and echoes the pillar of 28:18.

system_instances.outcome_summary: As God Almighty, God promises Israel a nation, a company of nations, kings, and the land given to Abraham and Isaac.
system_instances.significance_note: It passes the Abrahamic promises of offspring and land on to Jacob.

system_instances.outcome_summary: A terror from God falls on the surrounding cities and no one pursues Jacob's sons.
system_instances.significance_note: It shows God protecting Jacob after the Shechem massacre, in the way he said he would.

edges.description: God blesses Jacob when he appears to him again on his return from Paddan-aram.
God commands Jacob to go up to Bethel, settle there and make an altar.
God promises Israel and his offspring the land he gave to Abraham and Isaac.
God says Jacob's name will be Israel and no longer Jacob.
A terror from God falls on the cities round about so they do not pursue Jacob's sons.
Jacob pours a drink offering and oil on the stone pillar at Bethel.
Jacob buries his father Isaac beside Esau.
Jacob orders his household to put away foreign gods, purify themselves and change clothes.
Jacob buries the household's foreign gods under the oak by Shechem.
Jacob sets up a pillar over Rachel's grave.
Jacob calls the baby Benjamin instead.
The midwife tells Rachel not to fear, for she has another son.
Dying, Rachel calls the baby Ben-oni.
Reuben lies with Bilhah, his father's concubine, an affront to his father.
